questions.question: What replaced Universal Analytics as Google's primary analytics platform?
questions.explanation: GA4 replaced Universal Analytics in July 2023. It uses an event-based model instead of session-based, tracks across web and app, and has built-in machine learning.

questions.question: In GA4, what is an 'event'?
options: Any user interaction tracked on your website or app (page view, click, purchase, scroll)
questions.explanation: GA4 tracks everything as events — page_view, scroll, click, purchase, form_submit, etc. Custom events can be created for any specific interaction you want to measure.

questions.question: Which attribution model gives 100% credit to the last touchpoint before conversion?
questions.explanation: Last-click attribution assigns all conversion credit to the final interaction before purchase. It's simple but ignores the role of earlier touchpoints in the customer journey.

questions.question: A customer's journey: saw Instagram ad (Day 1) → clicked Google ad (Day 5) → clicked email link (Day 10) → purchased. In linear attribution, how is credit distributed?
options: 50% to Google ad, 25% each to others
questions.explanation: Linear attribution distributes credit equally across all touchpoints. With 3 touchpoints, each gets 33.3% credit — useful when every interaction matters equally.

questions.question: What is a UTM parameter?
options: Tags added to URLs to track the source, medium, and campaign of traffic in analytics
questions.explanation: UTM parameters (utm_source, utm_medium, utm_campaign, utm_content, utm_term) are added to URLs so analytics tools can identify exactly where traffic comes from.

questions.question: Which UTM parameter identifies the platform sending traffic (e.g., google, facebook, newsletter)?
questions.explanation: utm_source identifies the traffic source (google, facebook, linkedin). utm_medium identifies the type (cpc, email, social). They work together for full tracking.

questions.question: What does Microsoft Clarity or Hotjar's heatmap show you?
options: Where users click, scroll, and move their mouse on your pages
questions.explanation: Heatmaps visualize user behavior — click maps show where people click, scroll maps show how far they scroll, and move maps show cursor movement patterns.

questions.question: What is Looker Studio (formerly Google Data Studio) used for?
options: Creating visual dashboards and reports by connecting multiple data sources
questions.explanation: Looker Studio connects to GA4, Google Ads, Sheets, BigQuery, etc. to create interactive visual dashboards that update automatically — essential for client reporting.

questions.question: In time-decay attribution, which touchpoint gets the MOST credit?
options: The touchpoint closest to the conversion
The touchpoint with the highest cost
questions.explanation: Time-decay gives increasing credit to touchpoints closer to conversion. The logic: recent interactions had more influence on the final purchase decision.

questions.question: A digital marketing freelancer charges ₹25,000/month retainer for managing social media and ads for a local restaurant. What pricing model is this?
questions.explanation: Retainer pricing charges a fixed monthly fee for ongoing services. It provides predictable income for the freelancer and consistent support for the client.

questions.question: What is a marketing pitch deck?
options: A presentation that communicates your marketing strategy, capabilities, and proposed plan to a client or stakeholder
questions.explanation: A pitch deck (10-15 slides) presents your understanding of the client's problem, proposed strategy, expected results, timeline, and pricing to win business.

questions.question: Which data-driven attribution model uses machine learning to assign credit based on actual conversion data?
questions.explanation: Data-driven attribution uses machine learning algorithms to analyze your actual conversion paths and assign credit based on which touchpoints truly influenced conversions.

questions.question: What is competitive intelligence in digital marketing?
options: Systematically gathering and analyzing information about competitors' strategies, keywords, and positioning
Reporting competitors to Google for policy violations
Buying competitor brand names as keywords
questions.explanation: Competitive intelligence involves using tools (SEMrush, SimilarWeb, SpyFu) to analyze competitor keywords, ad spend, traffic sources, and content strategy to find opportunities.

questions.question: A startup has ₹3,00,000 monthly marketing budget. They allocate 50% to paid ads, 30% to content, and 20% to tools. How much goes to content?
questions.explanation: Content budget = 30% of ₹3,00,000 = ₹90,000. Budget allocation should align with business goals — startups often spend more on paid ads for quick results.

questions.question: What should an ATS-optimized resume for a digital marketing role include?
options: Relevant keywords from the job description, quantified achievements, and a clean format
questions.explanation: ATS (Applicant Tracking Systems) scan resumes for keywords. Use terms from the JD, quantify results ('increased leads by 40%'), and keep formatting simple — no columns or graphics.

questions.question: Which GA4 metric shows the percentage of sessions that had no meaningful engagement?
questions.explanation: In GA4, bounce rate = sessions that were not 'engaged sessions.' An engaged session lasts 10+ seconds, has 2+ page views, or has a conversion event.

questions.question: What is the advantage of hourly billing vs retainer for a freelance digital marketer?
options: Hourly billing always earns more money
Hourly billing is fair for unpredictable scope work; retainer provides stable monthly income
There is no difference between the two
questions.explanation: Hourly works when scope is unclear (consulting, audits). Retainers suit ongoing work (monthly ads/SEO management) and give both sides predictability.

questions.question: A client asks how your proposed campaign will perform. What forecasting method uses historical data from similar past campaigns?
options: Guessing based on industry averages only
Using past campaign data and trend analysis to project future results
questions.explanation: Forecasting uses historical performance data, seasonality trends, and industry benchmarks to project realistic results. Never guarantee exact outcomes — provide ranges.

questions.question: Which AI tool can help marketers generate ad copy variations quickly?
questions.explanation: AI tools like ChatGPT, Claude, and Jasper can generate multiple ad copy variants, email subject lines, and content ideas — saving time while requiring human review and editing.

questions.question: What is the key difference between freelancing and agency employment for a digital marketer?
options: Freelancers manage their own clients, income, and schedule; employees get stability, benefits, and team support
There is no difference in work type
Agency employees never interact with clients
questions.explanation: Freelancing offers flexibility and higher earning potential but requires self-discipline, client acquisition, and no benefits. Employment provides stability, team learning, and fixed income.
